body:
## Motivation

On a prefix match the matched node's mamba snapshot is copied into the request's own mamba slot, so during decode the request reads its own slot and never touches the tree node's mamba. Keeping that node mamba-locked through decode pins one pool slot per running request for nothing. This PR leaves it evictable during decode by acquiring the decode-time re-lock with the mamba component skipped, which frees one resident mamba slot per running request and lets the extra-buffer pool ratios shrink (overlap 5 to 4, overlap-lazy 4 to 3).

The optimization is gated behind `SGLANG_OPT_MAMBA_SKIP_DECODE_LOCK` (default off), so the PR is purely additive: with the flag off, locking and the pool ratio are byte-identical to `main`. With the flag on, for the overlap-lazy strategy at a 96-slot mamba pool this lifts `max_running_requests` from 24 to 32 (**33%**) with **20%** higher output throughput at concurrency 200.

## Modifications

- `inc_lock_ref` gains a component-generic `skip_lock_components`. When `SGLANG_OPT_MAMBA_SKIP_DECODE_LOCK` is set, the decode-time re-lock in `cache_unfinished_req` passes `(ComponentType.MAMBA,)`, acquiring full only and recording the skipped node ids in `IncLockRefResult.skip_lock_node_ids`, carried on the request as `Req.skip_lock_node_ids`. The only mamba-specific mention is that one call site.
- The flag also gates the pool ratio in `_calculate_mamba_ratio`: off keeps the base at 3 (overlap 5, lazy 4, no_buffer 3), on drops it to 2 (overlap 4, lazy 3) while no_buffer stays 3. Skip and ratio move together so the pool is never undersized. With the flag off the skip set is empty, so the dec paths below are all no-ops and behavior matches `main` exactly.
- Every path that releases the request's `last_node` honors that skip set so it never drops a lock it did not take (which may be another request's on a shared node): `cache_finished_req` (incl. retract) and the `cache_unfinished_req` re-lock swap both go through a new `_dec_req_lock` helper, plus `dec_swa_lock_only` and the streaming-session `release_session`.
- The skip records tombstone nodes (value is None) too, matching `acquire_component_lock`, so a revived tombstone later locked by another request is not wrongly decremented.
- `SessionSlot` carries `skip_lock_node_ids` across turns so the streaming path, which handles finish before the raw dec, does not bypass the skip.
- Mamba pool ratio base drops 3 to 2. `no_buffer` adds it back to stay at effective 3 because its binding constraint is the prefill to decode transition peak (own slot + admission-locked prefix + donated slot), which the decode-time drop does not shrink and which its leaf-only mode has no ping-pong headroom to absorb.
- `SWARadixCache.dec_swa_lock_only` signature is aligned with the unified cache so the shared call site cannot `TypeError` if that backend is ever registered.

## Correctness

The change is confined to one axis: whether a tree node's cached mamba is protected from radix eviction during a request's decode. It moves no state copy, touches no ping-pong buffer, and adds no cross-stream op, so it does not interact with mamba state copy ordering.

A tree node's mamba is immutable once inserted and has exactly one kind of reader: a request performing the match-time copy-on-write from that node into its own slot. That request holds an admission full-lock (mamba included) on the node for the whole window from recording the source to executing the copy. The copy source is that request's own `last_node` (a device-resident mamba source is the deepest device match, which is `last_node`), it is recorded only if still resident, and it is re-locked before the next allocation can evict it. The decoding request that produced the node reads its own copied slot and never the tree node, so its former decode-time mamba lock was redundant protection. A node that is nobody's active copy source is safe to leave evictable.

The dependency this introduces: safety now rests on those scheduler invariants (source is `last_node`, recorded only if resident, locked before the next alloc) rather than on the redundant decode-time lock. A scheduler that matched a whole batch before locking would break it, so a comment at the skip site pins the contract.

## Usage

Off by default. Enable per deployment with the env var:

```bash
SGLANG_OPT_MAMBA_SKIP_DECODE_LOCK=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <hybrid-mamba-model> ...
```

Unset it (or `=0`) to fall back to the original locking and pool ratio.

## Accuracy

gsm8k and mmlu are unchanged (KL flat): gsm8k 0.970, mmlu 0.906.

Real-retract stress across all three mamba-radix strategies (small `--max-total-tokens` forcing KV retraction mid-decode) is crash-free with every request served:

```
extra_buffer_lazy : successful 256/256  crash 0  real retracts 76
extra_buffer      : successful 256/256  crash 0  real retracts 76
no_buffer         : successful 256/256  crash 0  real retracts 68
```

## Benchmark

Launch (overlap-lazy, 96-slot mamba pool), main vs this PR differ only in the pool ratio:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \
  --tp 4 --trust-remote-code --context-len 16384 \
  --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy --mamba-track-interval 256 \
  --max-mamba-cache-size 96 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --enable-cache-report
```

```bash
python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --model Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 128 \
  --random-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 1200 --max-concurrency 200
```

main branch:

```
max_running_requests: 24
Request throughput (req/s):       22.25
Output token throughput (tok/s):  2847.90
Mean TTFT (ms):                   7334.24
```

this PR:

```
max_running_requests: 32
Request throughput (req/s):       26.68
Output token throughput (tok/s):  3414.96
Mean TTFT (ms):                   5843.56
```

## Tests

- `test_streaming_session_unit.py::test_release_session_threads_mamba_skip_ids` fails before the session fix and passes after.
- `test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.py` pins the sizing floor: at the prefill peak (N locked distinct prefixes + N own slots) a pool of 2N has no evictable victim and the donated alloc asserts, 3N has headroom, and once decode leaves the prefix evictable even 2N recovers by eviction.
